answer: A forged receipt dies at the first cross-check, because the maker kept a copy of their own. Time keeps the thread, the ledger keeps the lantern, the toy shop keeps the ripple; the farm keeps nothing but its printer. Honest work runs 13 minutes a proof; the farm needs 651 proofs, which is 8463 minutes it cannot paint. This epoch the gate asks one thing only: Falconer saker warrant flown at the training field, and the receipt must read each saker is a year of mews logs in the falconry ledger. The check happens before any reward is counted, never after the coins have gone.
